qa.question: Should the owners of LSP-Whitewater change to the We Energies companies?
qa.finding: A 2022 commission decision approved a 50-50 purchase by Wisconsin Electric Power Company and Wisconsin Public Service Corporation, and a We Energies fact sheet says the plant was bought in 2023. EIA lists Wisconsin Electric Power Co.
qa.recommendation: Confirm the closing and the shares in the 2023 utility filings, then replace the four former owners with the buyers. Until then leave the owner list as it is.
qa.note:
The owner list for this plant may be out of date.

What the sources say:
- The Public Service Commission of Wisconsin final decision at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=455168 (docket 5-BS-264, decision dated November 2022, page 1) says it grants Wisconsin Electric Power Company and Wisconsin Public Service Corporation authority to buy the LSP-Whitewater facility. The paragraph under 'Introduction' says 'each applicant would acquire 50 percent of the Whitewater facility's capacity'. I read the full decision at that address.
- A We Energies fact sheet at https://www.we-energies.com/company/pdf/whitewater-generating-station.pdf says on page 1, under 'Initial cost', that 'We Energies purchased the power plant from LSP Whitewater in 2023 for $75 million'. It does not name Wisconsin Public Service Corporation.
- The EIA-860M table for September 2026 at https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx lists plant 55011, generators CTG1 and STG1, under the entity Wisconsin Electric Power Co.

What was not found: a document that states the closing date or the final shares. The owner list in GEM still shows the former LSP-Whitewater partners.

proposed_value.Owner(s): Wisconsin Electric Power Company [50%]; Wisconsin Public Service Corporation [50%]

qa.question: Is 284 MW the right capacity when the commission decision says 236.5 MW?
qa.finding: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 gives nameplate 177.3 MW plus 106.2 MW, which is 283.5 MW. The commission decision at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=455168 gives 236.5 MW AC for the facility, and the We Energies fact sheet gives 280 MW net.
qa.recommendation: Leave 284 MW, which matches EIA nameplate. The lower figures are net or alternating current ratings.
